subtext: Built, rebuilt and tested by engineers who work on Land Rover engines every day.
Here's our practical view of the Td5 across its Land Rover applications.

columns.title: APPLICATIONS WE SEE:
columns.body: The Td5 is found in two core Land Rover model lines — the Defender (L316) and the Discovery 2 (L318).

columns.title: WHAT WE REPLACE:
columns.body: Timing chain, bearings, and gaskets as standard on every rebuild, with the injector wiring harness being a critical component we inspect and often replace due to known issues.

columns.title: KNOWN ISSUES:
columns.body: The Td5 has well-documented issues with injector wiring harness oil wicking and injector seal leakage. We address these as part of our standard rebuild scope.

notice.rest: engine-specific case studies with real job details are not yet included on this page — they'll be added once a documented set of completed Td5 rebuilds is available to draw from, rather than filled with placeholder examples now.

typical.title: LAND ROVER Td5 REBUILD
typical.intro: The following describes a typical rebuild scope for this engine — illustrative of the work involved, not a specific customer job. Real case studies from our own completed work will replace this section once available.
typical.body: The Td5 is a common-rail diesel engine with a chain-driven timing system. A full rebuild includes inspecting the injector harness for oil wicking — a known critical issue — and replacing it if necessary. Injector seal replacement is also standard practice. The high-pressure fuel pump and turbocharger are inspected for condition.

scope.label: Typical Scope:
scope.text: Timing chain, bearings, gaskets, injector wiring harness inspection/replacement, injector seals
